title: 100 Objects #21: Window from the House of D

sentences.en: Are you rolling, Marty?
sentences.zh: 玛蒂，你在录音吗？

sentences.en: This is Audra Lorde, the celebrated writer and poet.
sentences.zh: 这位是奥德丽·洛德，著名的作家和诗人。

sentences.en: She's being interviewed here for an oral history about Greenwich Village.
sentences.zh: 她在这里接受采访，讲述格林威治村的口述历史。

sentences.en: It's a neighborhood in lower Manhattan that today is one of the most famously gay places in the country.
sentences.zh: 这是曼哈顿下城的一个社区，如今这里是全美最著名的同性恋聚集地之一。

sentences.en: Think Rainbow Crosswalks, the Stonewall Inn.
sentences.zh: 想想彩虹人行横道和石墙酒吧。

sentences.en: But back when Audra moved there in the late 40s, it was just starting to get that reputation.
sentences.zh: 但早在40年代末奥德丽搬到那里时，这里才刚刚开始享有这种声誉。

sentences.en: The village was the place where the outsiders went.
sentences.zh: 这个村庄是局外人去的地方。

sentences.en: The place, the artists, the funny people.
sentences.zh: 属于艺术家和怪咖的地方。

sentences.en: Audra had long known that she was one of the funny people.
sentences.zh: 奥德丽早就知道自己是个怪咖。

sentences.en: Queer.
sentences.zh: 酷儿。

sentences.en: A black poet in an all-white high school.
sentences.zh: 一所全白人高中里的黑人诗人。

sentences.en: So at 17, she left home for good.
sentences.zh: 所以在17岁时，她彻底离家出走了。

sentences.en: I came to the idea of a lesbian community, of gay girls through the village.
sentences.zh: 我是通过这个村庄了解到女同性恋社区和同性恋女孩的概念的。

sentences.en: Through my friends and I going down and going to Washington Square Park and trying to decide, you know, is she one?
sentences.zh: 通过我和朋友们经常去华盛顿广场公园，试图去判断，你知道的，她是吗？

sentences.en: You know, is she?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她是吗？

sentences.en: The way she describes the village, it has this dreamy, out-of-time quality to it.
sentences.zh: 她对这个村庄的描述带有一种梦幻般的、超越时间的特质。

sentences.en: It was a place you went to be free.
sentences.zh: 这是一个让你去获得自由的地方。

sentences.en: To be free on the streets.
sentences.zh: 在街上获得自由。

sentences.en: To be able to hold hands, you know.
sentences.zh: 能够手牵着手，你知道的。

sentences.en: And no one would bother you.
sentences.zh: 没有人会打扰你。

sentences.en: You could walk through with a flower in your hair, you know, and not be accosted.
sentences.zh: 你可以头上插着一朵花走过，你知道的，而不会遭到骚扰。

sentences.en: And then, about 20 minutes in, the interviewer changes the subject.
sentences.zh: 然后，在大约20分钟后，采访者转换了话题。

sentences.en: Tell me about the House of Detention.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲看守所的事吧。

sentences.en: The Women's House of Detention.
sentences.zh: 女子看守所。

sentences.en: And you'd think the mood would shift.
sentences.zh: 你可能会以为气氛会发生变化。

sentences.en: But it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但并没有。

sentences.en: The Women's House of Detention on 11th Street.
sentences.zh: 位于11街的女子看守所。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Well, I didn't know very much about the Women's House of Detention, except it was a real presence in our lives.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我对女子看守所知之甚少，只知道它对我们的生活产生了切切实的影响。

sentences.en: The Women's House of Detention was New York City's very first prison for women.
sentences.zh: 女子看守所是纽约市第一座女性监狱。

sentences.en: Smack dab in the middle of the village.
sentences.zh: 就坐落在村庄的正中央。

sentences.en: Audra herself was never locked up there.
sentences.zh: 奥德丽本人从未被关押在那里。

sentences.en: But that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但关键就在这里。

sentences.en: She didn't have to be, to really know the place.
sentences.zh: 她不需要被关进去，也能真正了解这个地方。

sentences.en: The prison, or the House of Detention, as it was called, had a way of spilling out onto the street.
sentences.zh: 这座监狱，或者说被称为看守所的地方，有一种向外延伸到街道上的魔力。

sentences.en: Because there was this thing about the windows.
sentences.zh: 因为这些窗户有个特点。

sentences.en: They opened.
sentences.zh: 它们是能打开的。

sentences.en: And the Women's House of Detention had a real life of its own.
sentences.zh: 而且女子看守所本身就有着充满生机的生活。

sentences.en: Because total conversations would go on, particularly in weekend nights, if you stood across Greenwich Avenue
sentences.zh: 因为人们会进行完整的对话，特别是在周末的晚上，如果你站在格林威治大道对面

sentences.en: and yelled up to the women in the upper stories, and they would be communicating.
sentences.zh: 朝着高楼层的女囚大喊，她们就会进行交流。

sentences.en: So, there was always a sense of this being another kind of outlawry that we were somehow connected with.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们总会觉得这是一种另类的叛逆，而我们不知怎么地与它联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And the scene of the women yelling down to the street, and the streets yelling back up?
sentences.zh: 至于女人朝街上大喊，街道又朝上面大喊的场景呢？

sentences.en: It wasn't just Audra who took note of it.
sentences.zh: 不只是奥德丽注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: Every single person that I talked to about Greenwich Village in these years and about the House of Detention,
sentences.zh: 我谈到格林威治村的这些年以及关于看守所时，遇到的每一个人

sentences.en: that's what they remembered.
sentences.zh: 他们记住的都是这个。

sentences.en: The women calling down and the people calling back up.
sentences.zh: 女人们向下呼喊，人们向上回应。

sentences.en: That's historian Hugh Ryan.
sentences.zh: 那是历史学家休·瑞安。

sentences.en: He spent years digging through the archives to write the first full history of the House of Detention.
sentences.zh: 他花了数年时间翻阅档案，写成了关于看守所的第一部完整历史。

sentences.en: And he says none of this was supposed to happen.
sentences.zh: 他说，这一切本不该发生。

sentences.en: All that talk between the prison and the street,
sentences.zh: 监狱和街道之间的所有那些对话，

sentences.en: it was just a side effect of the choice to install a particular type of window.
sentences.zh: 不过是选择安装某种特定类型窗户的副作用。

sentences.en: They wanted a window that looked like a normal city window.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一扇看起来像普通城市窗户的窗户。

sentences.en: Originally, they were supposed to be a sort of kindness, a way to signal that the place was for rehabilitation, not punishment.
sentences.zh: 最初，它们应该是一种善意，一种表明这个地方是为了改造而非惩罚的信号。

sentences.en: Hugh brought in an advertisement from the 30s to give a better sense of what the windows looked like.
sentences.zh: 休找来了一份30年代的广告，以便更好地让人了解这些窗户是什么样子的。

sentences.en: In the advert, it shows like a little piece of the window opening up, sort of cantilevers out.
sentences.zh: 广告显示，窗户的一小部分可以打开，有点向外悬挑。

sentences.en: It was meant to be open for ventilation.
sentences.zh: 它的设计初衷是为了通风开启。

sentences.en: Was communication and talking to people on the street like part of the calculation,
sentences.zh: 与街上的人交流和说话是考量的一部分吗，

sentences.en: or do you think this was just an oversight?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为这只是一种疏忽？

sentences.en: Total oversight.
sentences.zh: 完全是疏忽。

sentences.en: The windows don't start for a couple floors up because they thought that would be significant distance to keep people from communicating out.
sentences.zh: 窗户从好几层楼高的地方才开始设立，因为他们认为这是一个足以阻止人们向外交流的显著距离。

sentences.en: They didn't realize when you're desperate and you've been trapped inside an overcrowded cage for months on end,
sentences.zh: 他们没有意识到，当你绝望了，被困在一个过度拥挤的笼子里长达数月之久，

sentences.en: you are willing to shout below down to anyone out there,
sentences.zh: 你就会愿意对下面外面的任何人呐喊，

sentences.en: whether it's the person you intend to talk to,
sentences.zh: 无论那是不是你打算交谈的人，

sentences.en: whether you are sharing your deepest, darkest secrets,
sentences.zh: 无论你是在分享你内心最深、最黑暗的秘密，

sentences.en: or whether you are just yelling so that someone recognizes that you are still alive.
sentences.zh: 还是你只是在大喊，好让别人认出你还活着。

sentences.en: Those windows were the single most important thing about the building.
sentences.zh: 那些窗户是这栋建筑最重要的事情。

sentences.en: For the next 40 years, the women inside the house of D shouted down and the neighborhood shouted back.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的40年里，看守所里的女人们向下呐喊，社区也报以呐喊。

sentences.en: And Hugh argues that the fact that this prison sat in the mecca of gay America isn't a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 休认为，这座监狱坐落在美国同性恋的圣地并非巧合。

sentences.en: That the prison itself, with its special windows, actually played a major role,
sentences.zh: 这座监狱本身凭借其特殊的窗户，实际上发挥了重大的作用，

sentences.en: stick with me here,
sentences.zh: 听我把话说完，

sentences.en: in making the village queer.
sentences.zh: 让这个村庄变成了酷儿聚集地。

sentences.en: From 99% Invisible and BBC Studios,
sentences.zh: 来自“99%隐形”和BBC工作室，

sentences.en: this is a history of the United States in 100 Objects.
sentences.zh: 这里是“通过100件物品看美国历史”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Today, the windows in the house of D.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们聚焦看守所的窗户。

sentences.en: So the story that we're going to tell today is about the first women's prison in New York City.
sentences.zh: 所以我们今天要讲述的故事关于纽约市的第一座女子监狱。

sentences.en: But I want to back up like decades before that,
sentences.zh: 但我想把时间倒回几十年前，

sentences.en: because there was a time when we didn't send women to prison at all.
sentences.zh: 因为曾几何时，我们根本不把女性送进监狱。

sentences.en: Prison was only meant for men.
sentences.zh: 监狱原本只属于男性。

sentences.en: Could you describe this?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: So the history of incarceration in America is interesting,
sentences.zh: 美国的监禁历史很有趣，

sentences.en: because before basically the Civil War,
sentences.zh: 因为基本上在内战之前，

sentences.en: the places where we incarcerated people were mostly meant to handle the violent actions of white men.
sentences.zh: 我们关押犯人的地方主要是为了处理白人男性的暴力行为。

sentences.en: Women and people of color were rarely incarcerated because punishment and detention was handled through the nuclear family.
sentences.zh: 女性和有色人种很少被关进监狱，因为惩罚和拘留是由核心家庭来处理的。

sentences.en: It was your husband.
sentences.zh: 那是你的丈夫。

sentences.en: If you were unmarried, it was your father or your brothers.
sentences.zh: 如果你未婚，那就是你的父亲或兄弟。

sentences.en: If you were an enslaved black woman, it was the family that owned you.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个被奴役的黑人女性，那就是拥有你的家庭。

sentences.en: And then with the Civil War, not only are enslaved women freed,
sentences.zh: 然后在内战爆发后，不仅被奴役的女性获得了解放，

sentences.en: but many, many, many white women move into the workforce,
sentences.zh: 而且许许多多的白人女性也进入了劳动力市场，

sentences.en: move into the kind of public lives that meant that they were now under the thumb of the state.
sentences.zh: 进入了那种意味着她们现在处于国家掌控之下的公共生活。

sentences.en: So there becomes this moment where there's a recognition that we need to create prisons for women
sentences.zh: 因此，这一时刻的到来让人认识到我们需要为女性建立监狱，

sentences.en: because women are being arrested.
sentences.zh: 因为女性正在被逮捕。

sentences.en: And what are they being arrested for?
sentences.zh: 她们因为什么被捕？

sentences.en: So women, particularly black women, but all working class women,
sentences.zh: 女性，尤其是黑人女性，但还有所有的工人阶级女性，

sentences.en: and particularly women who are judged to be unfeminine,
sentences.zh: 特别是那些被认为缺乏女性特质的女性，

sentences.en: start to get arrested for prostitution or disorder,
sentences.zh: 开始因卖淫或寻衅滋事而被捕，

sentences.en: which is a code word for prostitution.
sentences.zh: 这是卖淫的代名词。

sentences.en: In the late 1800s, there were four jobs that a woman could have.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪后期，女性只能从事四种职业。

sentences.en: Three of them were legal.
sentences.zh: 其中三种是合法的。

sentences.en: Wife, mother, and the raiser of children.
sentences.zh: 妻子、母亲和抚养孩子的人。

sentences.en: So nursemaids or nannies, maybe even some kinds of teachers.
sentences.zh: 所以是保姆或育儿嫂，甚至可能是某些种类的老师。

sentences.en: And then there was the one illegal job, prostitute.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一种非法的职业，妓女。

sentences.en: So, in the eyes of the law, any woman who was not feminine enough to be a wife,
sentences.zh: 因此，在法律眼中，任何不够女性化而无法成为妻子、

sentences.en: a mother, or a nursemaid to children,
sentences.zh: 母亲或儿童保姆的女性，

sentences.en: meaning any woman who talked back, wore pants, smoked, wanted an education,
sentences.zh: 也就是任何顶嘴、穿裤子、抽烟、想要受教育的女性，

sentences.en: could not have a legal job as a woman.
sentences.zh: 都无法作为女性拥有一份合法的工作。

sentences.en: And so she would inevitably end up on the streets where she would end up a prostitute.
sentences.zh: 因此她不可避免地会流落街头，最终成为一名妓女。

sentences.en: And so most of the arrests we see of women are for prostitution,
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到女性被捕的大多数原因都是卖淫，

sentences.en: and not because of the exchange for sex for money.
sentences.zh: 并且并非因为金钱交易的性行为。

sentences.en: In fact, in New York State, by the early 1900s,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在纽约州，到20世纪初，

sentences.en: they've written into the law that that is not part of this.
sentences.zh: 他们已经在法律中写明这并不在其中。

sentences.en: Prostitution is the common lewdness of women.
sentences.zh: 卖淫是女性共同的淫荡行为。

sentences.en: So it's not about anything that they've actually done?
sentences.zh: 所以这与她们实际做过的事无关？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 无关。

sentences.en: In every way, what is being built in the 19th century
sentences.zh: 从方方面面来看，19世纪正在建立的是

sentences.en: is a sort of anticipatory justice.
sentences.zh: 一种某种前瞻性的正义。

sentences.en: It's not about crimes that have been committed.
sentences.zh: 这与已经犯下的罪行无关。

sentences.en: It's about what might happen,
sentences.zh: 这关乎可能会发生的事，

sentences.en: what these women might do,
sentences.zh: 关乎这些女性可能会做什么，

sentences.en: or how they might be a burden on the state in the future.
sentences.zh: 或者她们未来将如何成为国家的负担。

sentences.en: This idea of criminalizing women's wayward behavior,
sentences.zh: 这种将女性反叛行为定为犯罪的想法，

sentences.en: it's part of a larger reform movement happening in the country,
sentences.zh: 是国内正在发生的一个更大规模改革运动的一部分，

sentences.en: one that is led by other women.
sentences.zh: 这场运动由其他女性领导。

sentences.en: They're called the social feminists.
sentences.zh: 她们被称为社会女权主义者。

sentences.en: These are the same people who will eventually bring us both
sentences.zh: 这些人正是最终为我们带来

sentences.en: the right to vote, the suffragettes, and the temperance movement.
sentences.zh: 投票权、女权运动和禁酒运动的人。

sentences.en: These women saw themselves as helping their fallen sisters, right?
sentences.zh: 这些女性认为自己是在帮助堕落的姐妹，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's a sympathetic movement, but it's a pitying movement.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场充满同情的运动，但也是一场带有怜悯的运动。

sentences.en: It's sort of a looking down upon while also offering a hand up.
sentences.zh: 这是一种既俯视对方又伸出援手的姿态。

sentences.en: They wanted to look at people and say,
sentences.zh: 她们想要看着人们说，

sentences.en: if we are going to reform them,
sentences.zh: 如果我们打算改造她们，

sentences.en: if a prison isn't a place where you go just to be punished,
sentences.zh: 如果监狱不只是一个让你去接受惩罚的地方，

sentences.en: if the institution is meant to improve the person inside it,
sentences.zh: 如果该机构旨在改善身处其中之人，

sentences.en: how do we do that?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何做到这一点？

sentences.en: And when it comes to women,
sentences.zh: 而当谈到女性时，

sentences.en: the way they determined to do that was
sentences.zh: 她们决定采取的方法是

sentences.en: to set up institutions whose job it is
sentences.zh: 建立一些机构，其职责是

sentences.en: to make women properly feminine.
sentences.zh: 让女性变得恰如其分地具有女性特质。

sentences.en: And by institutions, these women weren't just talking about prisons.
sentences.zh: 而说到这些机构，这些女性所指的不仅仅是监狱。

sentences.en: If they were going to save all the souls of their fallen sisters,
sentences.zh: 如果她们要拯救所有堕落姐妹的灵魂，

sentences.en: they needed to think bigger.
sentences.zh: 她们就需要把格局放大。

sentences.en: Men and women are so different from one another, right?
sentences.zh: 男女有别，对吧？

sentences.en: So they say women need their own kind of justice.
sentences.zh: 所以她们说女性需要她们自己特有的正义。

sentences.en: Which meant different laws, different prisons, and a different court.
sentences.zh: 这意味着不同的法律、不同的监狱和不同的法庭。

sentences.en: But building a prison from scratch took time and money.
sentences.zh: 但从零开始建造一座监狱需要时间和金钱。

sentences.en: So they decided to tackle the court firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以她们决定先从法庭入手。

sentences.en: And in 1910, they got it.
sentences.zh: 在1910年，她们成功了。

sentences.en: The city's first women's court.
sentences.zh: 该市第一座女子法庭。

sentences.en: Right in the center of Greenwich Village.
sentences.zh: 就位于格林威治村的中心。

sentences.en: And the thing to note about this new court
sentences.zh: 而关于这个新法庭，有一点值得注意

sentences.en: was that everything took place after dark.
sentences.zh: 那就是一切都在天黑后进行。

sentences.en: After 8pm and sometimes well into the morning.
sentences.zh: 晚上8点之后，有时甚至会持续到清晨。

sentences.en: And it becomes a thing that people go to.
sentences.zh: 而且这变成了一个人们会去的地方。

sentences.en: Upper class people go to watch these women.
sentences.zh: 上流社会的人去观看这些女性。

sentences.en: Oh, it doesn't just become a thing for people to go to.
sentences.zh: 哦，它可不仅仅是人们去逛逛那么简单。

sentences.en: It is built to be a thing for people to go to.
sentences.zh: 它的建造目的就是为了让人门前来此观光。

sentences.en: When they opened the night court, the women's court in 1910,
sentences.zh: 当他们在1910年开设这个夜间法庭，也就是妇女法庭时，

sentences.en: they built stadium-style seating.
sentences.zh: 他们修建了体育场风格的座位。

sentences.en: They handed out flyers.
sentences.zh: 他们散发传单。

sentences.en: They put out a theatrical sign outside it so that it would say standing room only or full.
sentences.zh: 他们在外面挂了一个戏院风格的招牌，好写上“仅售站票”或“客满”。

sentences.en: Like it was a theater.
sentences.zh: 就像它是一个剧院一样。

sentences.en: They convinced people to come down and visit.
sentences.zh: 他们说服人们下来参观。

sentences.en: And the spectacle, it moved faSt.
sentences.zh: 而且这种奇观，进展得极快。

sentences.en: A woman would be marched up to the bench.
sentences.zh: 一个女人会被押送到法官席前。

sentences.en: Tourists and tabloid reporters would ogle.
sentences.zh: 游客和小报记者会大饱眼福。

sentences.en: She'd plead guilty or be found guilty.
sentences.zh: 她会认罪或者被判有罪。

sentences.zh: 而在法庭开业后的10年内，

sentences.zh: 但在几乎所有方面，

sentences.zh: 我们今天所知的格林威治村正是这座法院的产物。
